subject: Civic Education
competence: Works with understanding the rights of the child and his duties.
lesson: Explains the importance of fulfilling the duties of rights of child: Rights-to-Development Case Audit and Impact Trial
unique_learning_outcome: Explains the importance of fulfilling the duties of rights of child.
Expresses how enjoying rights of child bring about child development.
the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: The teacher launches the session by projecting a chalkboard dilemma scenario contrasting a well-functioning local school library initiative with an unattended community playground. The teacher poses the driving prompt: 'How does fulfilling our duty to respect school rules and maintain educational resources directly unlock our right to development?' Students in their 9 desk islands engage in a 2-minute rapid buzz discussion, with Scribes noting initial hypotheses on scrap paper while Spokespersons share contrasting viewpoints on how rights and duties interconnect in daily Sri Lankan student life.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher circulates among the 9 desk islands, distributing the dual case studies on the chalkboard regarding a Sri Lankan school health program and a community library. The facilitator prompts the Civic Investigators and Secretaries with scaffolding questions: 'Examine how children's fulfillment of health and study duties directly impacts their developmental milestones.'
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students collaborate in their groups, assigning roles to dissect the case studies. Scribes record specific behavioral duties linked to the right to education and health, while Investigators verify textbook alignment regarding mutual responsibilities.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_method: Case Evidence Analysis and Scenario Scrutiny
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chalkboard case study texts, Student Notebooks, highlighters

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: Acting as a facilitator, the teacher monitors group drafting sessions across all desk islands, guiding Timekeepers on pacing and prompting Creative Directors to ensure clear visual categorization of developmental impacts.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Group members synthesize their audit findings into a structured 'Rights & Duties Audit Matrix' poster on chart paper. The Creative Director and Spokesperson coordinate to map out how fulfilling duties such as personal hygiene and discipline accelerates personal and community development.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chart Paper, Color Markers, Task Sheets

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher moderates a rapid 5-minute gallery rotation where teams review adjacent posters, posing probing inquiry questions to challenge assumptions about self-centered rights versus responsible development.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Spokespersons and team members examine peer audit posters, offering constructive feedback using sticky notes and verbal evaluations on how well the matrices explain the connection between duties and child development.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_method: Peer Review and Gallery Walk Synthesis

summary: The teacher orchestrates a 2-minute synthesis highlighting that rights without responsibilities are self-centred, confirming that fulfilling duties such as disciplined learning and health compliance directly drives holistic child development across Sri Lankan communities.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Formative assessment is conducted through observation of active group collaboration, accuracy of the Rights & Duties Audit Matrix posters, and the depth of peer evaluations during the gallery review regarding the connection between child duties and development.
post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: Pass-the-Parcel Concept Challenge: Students participate in an in-class active evaluation where a designated prompt box containing real-world developmental dilemma cards is passed across desk islands to lively rhythmic clapping. When the clapping stops, the student holding the parcel selects a card detailing a Sri Lankan child scenario, and their team has 60 seconds to articulate how fulfilling a specific duty secures the child's right to development, receiving immediate formative feedback from the facilitator.
selected_activity:
Activity: Rights-to-Development Case Audit and Impact Trial
Approach: Students conduct a guided case audit of fictionalized yet realistic Sri Lankan community scenarios to evaluate the direct link between fulfilling child duties and achieving positive developmental milestones.
Student task: Teams audit two case studies provided on the chalkboard regarding children in local environments (e.g., a school health program or a community library initiative). Investigators and scribes examine how mutual duties support these rights, drafting a consensus audit report on chart paper.
Teacher facilitation: The teacher circulates among the 9 desk islands, ensuring all 50 students actively contribute through their rotating roles, keeping time for the audit phases, and steering discussions toward specific developmental outcomes.
Expected output: A completed 'Rights & Duties Audit Matrix' poster outlining developmental impacts for children.
Grouping: 9 teams (4 groups of 5, 5 groups of 6) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer, Creative Director / Chart Lead
